name: Revoke a runner key
description: Admin only, and only over the caller's own keys. Revocation is the mechanism this design leans on instead of short credentials: a runner's ten-minute token expires on its own, but every runner statement JOINs live_runners, which reads through to this row -- so stamping revoked_at here stops every machine started from this key on its NEXT call, not at the end of some window. Matches those machines are holding are not cancelled; their leases lapse and the reap returns them to the queue, which is the same path a crash takes.

with.name: Admins only
with.description: The role is read off the live session rather than off a claim in the cookie, so revoking a session or demoting a user takes effect on the next request.

tasks.name: Revoke
tasks.description: The ownership check IS the WHERE clause, so there is no diagnosing read: a key that is not yours and a key that does not exist are one answer on purpose, and an already-revoked key is the same 404 rather than a second state to explain.

input.query: UPDATE runner_keys k SET revoked_at = now() FROM users u JOIN live_sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id AND s.sid = ($3)::uuid WHERE k.id = ($2)::uuid AND k.user_id = u.id AND u.id = ($1)::uuid AND u.role = 'admin' AND k.revoked_at IS NULL
